summary: Brother of Temperance Smith and John's 7th-great-grand-uncle; captain of the Woodbury Clove militia company in Orange County, New York.
bio: Austin Smith was a brother of Temperance Smith, which makes him John's 7th-great-grand-uncle. He was a public man of Woodbury Clove in Orange County, New York. In 1765 he and John Earl served as overseers of roads for the Clove, in 1771 he was captain of the Woodbury Clove military company, and in 1775 he was fence-viewer and assessor. The Upper Clove company was afterwards described as the one 'formerly commanded by Capt. Austin Smith'. He married Mehitable Tuthill, a daughter of James Tuthill and sister of John Tuthill, the husband of his sister Temperance. He signed the Articles of Association in Cornwall Precinct in 1775, but he later sided with the Crown: he died a Loyalist in 1798, and at least two of his sons went with him to Annapolis County, Nova Scotia.
sources: [R4-S1] C. H. Weygant, The Family Record (1897; devoted to the Sackett, Weygant and Mapes families and intersecting lines), pp. 144-145, 'Smiths of Smithtown', Generations III-V (secondary) https://archive.org/details/familyrecor00weyg

researchNotes:
The Upper Clove company was 'formerly commanded by Capt. Austin Smith'. Fence-viewer and assessor for Woodbury Clove in 1775.

Weygant (1897): in 1765 Austin Smith and John Earl were 'Overseers of Roads for Woodbury Clove', and in 1771 Austin was captain of the Woodbury Clove military company ([R4-S1]). WikiTree gives his wife as Mehitable Tuthill (unverified).

F. K. Smith (1967) no. 102: 'Austin, m. Mehitable Tuthill, settled in the southeastern part of Orange County, N.Y., about twenty [years before the Revolution]'; 'at least two sons were with him, in Annapolis County' [Nova Scotia]; Mehitable 'daughter of James and ___ Tuthill'. The Home-Nest Chronicles descendant chart gives 'Austin Smith (Loyalist) 1728–1798 + Mehitable Tuthill 1728–'. The death place in Nova Scotia is inferred from F. K. Smith and the Loyalist label; no death record seen. His Loyalist claim (UK National Archives AO 12/13; Library and Archives Canada; Ancestry 'UK, American Loyalist Claims') is unread and may name his Woodbury Clove in-laws. He signed the 1775 Cornwall Articles of Association (Ruttenber & Clark pp. 68–69).
funFacts: He signed the patriot Articles of Association in 1775 while his brother Francis led the Woodbury Clove militia, yet Austin ended his days a Loyalist in Nova Scotia.
